investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes are excluded by affinity rules and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every remote agent pod creation attempt stalls as Unschedulable, the VM is never assigned, and the eval probe times out without writing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval runner or source code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots on those nodes are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, creating a hard capacity ceiling. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive (e.g., targeting a specific node pool that is undersized), adding capacity to the wrong node pool would not resolve the issue.

Tertiary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit set too low at the namespace or node level: the extended resource ceiling may be configured below actual hardware capacity, artificially constraining how many VM-backed pods can run concurrently.

Lower probability — a concurrent workload spike consumed all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots immediately before the eval run, causing a transient exhaustion rather than a persistent capacity shortfall. The fact that all three sibling checks failed across a ~7-minute window (19:49–19:56 UTC) makes a brief transient less likely but not impossible.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-19T19:51–19:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were produced, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" for every remote-agent pod the eval attempted to create. The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource — which backs the Swarm VM sandbox required for remote agent provisioning — is exhausted on both eligible nodes, and preemption found no victims to free capacity. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) could not complete, so the probe exited with the scheduler error message and produced an empty evidence object, violating all four required evidence fields defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the only two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Preemption found no lower-priority victims, confirming no automatic relief path.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy (likely the kata peer-pods node pool). If the node pool was recently scaled down or nodes were cordoned/drained, the eligible node count may have decreased, compounding the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — Concurrent load or leaked eval agents: if prior eval runs or production workloads did not clean up remote agent VMs, those VMs may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crashed run could leave orphaned VMs.

LOW PROBABILITY — Cluster-level quota or resource limit change: a recent change to ResourceQuota or LimitRange for the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource could have reduced the allocatable count on the two eligible nodes, but no such change is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes are excluded by affinity rules and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every remote agent pod creation attempt stalls as Unschedulable, the VM is never assigned, and the eval probe times out without writing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval runner or source code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, creating a hard capacity ceiling. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive (e.g., targeting a specific node pool that is undersized), adding capacity to the wrong node pool would not resolve the issue.

Tertiary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit set too low at the namespace or node level: the extended resource ceiling may be configured below actual hardware capacity, artificially constraining how many VM-backed pods can run concurrently.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned and the runtime response contract could not be satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity, and four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, no evidence was returned, and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents eval in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe pod. All three sibling checks report the same error, indicating this is a cluster-wide resource constraint at the time of the run.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, which may indicate a label mismatch, a node group that was scaled down, or a taint added to those nodes that prevents scheduling. This would reduce the effective scheduling domain to only the 2 kata-capable nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion is expected without a capacity increase or autoscaler configuration.

Lower confidence — node affinity rules in the pod spec are overly restrictive and do not match the current node topology, causing permanent rather than transient unschedulability on 4 of 6 nodes regardless of VM slot availability.

Evidence that the 4 affinity-excluded nodes were intentionally removed from the remote-agent scheduling domain (e.g., a deliberate label change) would disprove the drift hypothesis and confirm the pool is intentionally limited to 2 nodes.
